purpose: Adaptive development evidence for source-excerpt recall; not a held-out or live-user quality claim.
limitations: Six task pairs were initially run; the log-retention task lacked a return-type contract and is unscorable in both arms. It remains in the raw results.
Strict JSON formatting failed in 8/12 paired, 3/5 source-only and 2/5 store-format outputs. Offline execution removed only one outer Markdown fence; no code or JSON body repair.
Source-only and store-format runs were added after inspecting paired results, so results are adaptive rather than independent held-out evidence.
One controlled file-tree corruption was authored; other summaries came from the preceding actual model extraction outputs.
All inputs are synthetic and use one cached reference model, one seed and temperature zero. There is no native-only baseline, blind human review, real-user result or claim about all coding tasks.
The export-options task still fails: the model removes unrelated actions despite the exact source qualification.
Source excerpts can omit surrounding context. They do not repair inaccurate stored summaries or prove extraction faithfulness.
